questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Spin-Only Magnetic Moments of High/Low Spin
questions.category: d- and f-Block Elements :: Quantitative & Structural Chemistry (Type 1)
questions.question: In [d- and f-Block Elements], how does the basicity and reducing nature of orthophosphorous acid $(\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3)$ compare to orthophosphoric acid $(\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4)$?
options: $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$ is dibasic and a strong reducing agent due to one $\text{P-H}$ bond; $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ is tribasic and non-reducing
questions.solution: $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$ has tetrahedral coordination with two ionizable $-\text{OH}$ groups (dibasic) and one direct $\text{P-H}$ bond that imparts strong reducing properties. $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ has three $-\text{OH}$ groups (tribasic) and no $\text{P-H}$ bond (non-reducing).
questions.explanation: Analyze using fundamental chemical principles in d- and f-Block Elements.
tags: Spin-Only Magnetic Moments of High/Low Spin

questions.question: What is the basicity (number of ionizable hydrogen atoms per molecule) of pyrophosphoric acid $(\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7)$ in [d- and f-Block Elements]?
questions.solution: Pyrophosphoric acid contains two tetrahedral phosphorus atoms connected by a $\text{P-O-P}$ bridge, with four $-\text{OH}$ groups attached directly to phosphorus. All four hydrogens are acidic, so its basicity is $4$.
